weact.takeaway: An agent can change the weights it uses as a task unfolds. WeAct trains separate capability adapters and lets the agent activate them through tool calls, continuing from a shared interaction history.
weact.question: How can a long-horizon agent learn, combine and update different capabilities without forcing every stage of a task through one fixed parameter configuration?

method.title: Learn capabilities independently
method.text: Train Plan, Search and Writing LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone. Retain earlier interactions as context, but supervise only the current capability’s assistant outputs and exit call.

method.title: Make weights callable
method.text: Expose load_lora and offload_lora as native tools. At most one adapter is active; its weights govern subsequent reasoning and external tool use.

method.title: Expand or refine the library
method.text: Register a newly trained Code adapter or update the Writing adapter while keeping the backbone and the other adapters fixed.

findings.label: Mean accuracy across eight deep-research benchmarks
findings.detail: WeAct-hard improves on Full SFT’s 42.80% by 2.67 percentage points, a 6.2% relative gain. WeAct-soft averages 43.21%.

findings.label: Relative gain over the strongest static merge
findings.detail: WeAct-hard’s 45.47% versus TIES-Merging’s 35.66% is a 9.81-point difference. Both WeAct variants outperform every tested static merge on all eight benchmarks.

weact.scope: The main results use Qwen3-32B and a small library of three capability adapters. The paper’s uncertainty estimates are nominal task-based binomial standard errors, not variability across repeated training runs. Keeping other parameters unchanged prevents overwriting them, but does not establish retention within an updated adapter or stable routing through many successive updates. Scaling the library and defining capability boundaries for less structured tasks remain open questions.

Internal tool calls select the active weights, while external tools interact with the environment (bottom). WeAct-hard prescribes the stage order; WeAct-soft selects capabilities from the evolving history. The paths and percentages in this schematic illustrate execution, rather than benchmark measurements.

glance.result: 45.47% average accuracy across eight benchmarks, versus 42.80% for full fine-tuning.
glance.prior: Independently trained adapters become actions that change the agent’s active weights during a trajectory.
glance.limitation: Evaluated on one backbone with a small adapter library; sustained continual learning remains open.
